First Derivative Test for Local Extrema Suppose that c is a critical point of a continuous function ƒ, and that ƒ is differ- entiable at every point in some interval containing c except possibly at c itself. Moving across this interval from left to right,

1. if ƒ′ changes from negative to positive at c, then ƒ has a local minimum at c; 2. if ƒ′ changes from positive to negative at c, then ƒ has a local maximum at c; 3. if ƒ′ does not change sign at c (that is, ƒ′ is positive on both sides of c or negative on both sides), then ƒ has no local extremum at c.
The test for local extrema at endpoints is similar, but there is only one side to consider in determining whether ƒ is increasing or decreasing, based on the sign of ƒ′.
